title: Psychological Problems: Exam-Style Stretch
welcome_lead: Apply explanations of disorders to scenarios and evaluate them.
meta_desc: GCSE Psychology exam stretch on disorders: addiction explanations, evaluation and application.
final_note: You can argue using diathesis-stress and concordance evidence.

concepts.def: Pressure from friends to use substances.
Brain pathway that reinforces addictive behaviour.
Return to disorder after a period of recovery.

walkthroughs.body_html: Biological: genetic risk, abnormal dopamine reward pathways and tolerance. Social: peer pressure, modelling, availability and culture. Most modern models combine biological vulnerability with social triggers — a biopsychosocial view.
'Sam, 16, has not enjoyed anything for three weeks and feels worthless.' Suggest depression. Explain using Beck's negative triad and consider biological vulnerability. Recommend talking to a GP.

Strength: clear treatments map onto each explanation (SSRIs for biology, CBT for cognition). Weakness: reductionist if used alone; many cases need a combined approach. Cultural bias is also a concern in diagnosis.
